_source: Curated editorial picks based on real, verified 2025-26 Premier League season data (Premier League awards, Sky Sports, ESPN, Opta Analyst) plus confirmed 2026-27 form where noted. Not a live per-gameweek Fantasy Premier League feed — see docs/FOOTBALL-HUB.md.
note: Three picks per position, grounded in real 2025-26 season honours and stats — a curated "who to watch" guide, not a live fantasy-points tracker.

GK.name: David Raya
GK.note: Won a third straight Golden Glove in 2025-26 and started the new season as first choice behind the league's best defensive record.

GK.name: Gianluigi Donnarumma
GK.note: Kept 15 clean sheets in his debut Premier League season after joining Manchester City, finishing runner-up in the 2025-26 Golden Glove race.

GK.name: Bart Verbruggen
GK.note: Sharply improved shot-stopping numbers in 2025-26 made him one of the league's most in-form goalkeepers heading into 2026-27.

DEF.name: William Saliba
DEF.note: Anchored the league's meanest defence in Arsenal's title-winning 2025-26 campaign, one of the hardest defenders in the league to beat 1v1.

DEF.name: Gabriel Magalhães
DEF.note: In the conversation for Player of the Season for long spells of 2025-26 as one half of the league's best centre-back pairing.

DEF.name: Jurrien Timber
DEF.note: Converted from centre-back to a marauding right-back and was one of the league's standout defenders in Arsenal's title season.

MID.name: Bruno Fernandes
MID.note: Broke the Premier League single-season assists record in 2025-26 and won the Playmaker of the Season award by nine clear assists.

MID.name: Rayan Cherki
MID.note: A creative spark in his debut Premier League season at Manchester City, finishing second in the league's assists chart behind Bruno Fernandes.

MID.name: Martin Ødegaard
MID.note: Arsenal's captain and the engine of their 2025-26 title win, off the mark again with a goal in the 3-0 season-opening win over Coventry City.

FWD.name: Erling Haaland
FWD.note: Won a third Golden Boot in four seasons in 2025-26, five goals clear of nearest challenger Igor Thiago.

FWD.name: Igor Thiago
FWD.note: The breakout striker of 2025-26, finishing as the league's second-top scorer for newly ambitious Brentford.

FWD.name: Viktor Gyökeres
FWD.note: Scored 14 in his first Premier League season after a big-money move from Sporting CP, part of the title-winning Arsenal squad.
